skill.name: loop-me
skill.description: Guide a focused interview that turns repeated work into detailed workflow specifications inside the workspace.
skill.summary: Design implementation-ready workflow specs through one-question-at-a-time interviews.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Recurring work is hard to automate when requirements stay vague. This skill interviews you and turns each loop into a clear workspace spec.
actual_capabilities: Runs a stateful grilling session focused only on workflow specifications.
Asks one question at a time and includes a recommended answer.
Creates, edits, and deletes workflow specs as the interview resolves details.
Uses NOTES.md to capture terminology, tools, channels, and user context.
Identifies recurring loops and proposes workflows the user may not have noticed.
Checks that each spec is detailed enough for an implementer agent.
limitations: It designs workflow specs, but does not implement the automation itself.
It depends on accurate user answers and current workspace notes.
It focuses on local workspace files, not external service discovery.
It may need several questions before a workflow is ready.

use_cases.title: Clarify Repeated Personal Work
use_cases.description: Turn a recurring weekly or daily activity into a precise workflow spec.

use_cases.title: Prepare Automation Requirements
use_cases.description: Define triggers, checkpoints, briefs, and success criteria before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Capture Team Process Knowledge
use_cases.description: Record tools, channels, and team vocabulary while shaping repeatable workflow documents.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Workflow Interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a workflow for a recurring task in this workspace. Ask one question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Useful Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Look at my workspace context and interview me to find one repeated activity worth specifying.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the workflow specs in this workspace and grill me until one chosen spec is implementation-ready.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent-Ready Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my notes to define a workflow with clear triggers, checkpoints, briefs, edge cases, and done criteria.

output_examples.input: I want to automate my weekly inbox review.
output_examples.output: A workflow spec that defines the trigger, review goal, prepared brief, human checkpoint, and completion criteria.

output_examples.input: I have many repeated tasks but do not know where to start.
output_examples.output: A focused interview that identifies promising loops and selects one workflow to specify first.

output_examples.input: My workflow spec still has unclear terms.
output_examples.output: A tighter spec and updated workspace notes that explain the user's terminology for implementers.

best_practices: Start with one recurring activity that already consumes time or attention.
Keep NOTES.md current with real tools, channels, and local terminology.
Review each finished spec for missing triggers, checkpoints, and done criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a complete automation build when you only need a spec.
Do not skip the interview when the workflow has unclear ownership or vocabulary.
Do not create broad process documents that an implementer cannot act on.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates workflow specifications and supporting workspace notes for recurring work.

faq.question: Does it build the workflow automation?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the spec so another agent or developer can build the automation.

faq.question: Why does it ask one question at a time?
faq.answer: The interview format keeps the user focused and reduces vague requirements.

faq.question: Can it propose workflows for me?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use workspace context to suggest recurring loops worth specifying.

faq.question: Which files does it use?
faq.answer: It uses workflow spec files and NOTES.md within the workspace.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you need clear, implementation-ready requirements for repeated work.
